Q090-07.notes: Equal conditional probabilities iff grade total = ensemble total (joint count same). Grade totals 48, 60, 92 (sum 200); ensemble totals band 60, choir 70, orchestra 70. Grade 11 = band = 60. Others: A 42/92 vs 42/70; B 22/48 vs 22/70; C 18/60 vs 18/70.

flags: Easy elimination: A (geometry), C (prior-year grades), D (perceived helpfulness) are all obviously irrelevant to comparing A-rates of attenders vs non-attenders; only B mentions the comparison group. Consider a stronger distractor, e.g. 'the total number of students who attended the tutoring program' or 'the number of students who took algebra last year' (each insufficient alone).
Q090-08.notes: Need tutoring-attendance rate among non-A students (or equivalently A-rates by attendance group); B supplies the comparison baseline. Strictly B alone still needs group sizes to compute A-rates by attendance, but comparing 80% vs B's percent answers the 'more likely' question via Bayes direction, so B is defensible as most needed.
